I'll tell Leon the truth. He needs to talk things through with the Boss.
So, what do I think about this whole thing?
Time to head over to the theater to watch the final act of 'La Morte di Texas.'
If a bystander were here, he would have to wonder–who is this man?
Judge Lavinia seems to have something to say.
The courthouse is a great place to sleep. Hopefully nobody comes bothering me.
I ran into Ben outside on my way from the church.
Guess I'll head back to the famiglia then, and pay my respects to the Don.
The Don wants me back. I'll decide after I take a look around the new city.
Time to enjoy a show from the opera box.
Gonna talk to Ben again. Think I've figured some things out.
There are a few wise guys drinking at the bar. They seem to be discussing something.
Done washing the car. Now to tell the client.
I think I'll go people-watching to get some inspiration for my next script.
I hope Cellinia gets the chance to follow her heart.
I need to leave something behind for Cellinia.
Lots of unfinished work left on the schedule.
Time to deal with some famiglia business.
The performance went perfectly. I want the others to know how happy I am.
Now that the dust has settled, I'd like invite everyone to watch the performance of Act III.
I need to go somewhere real quick to get the materials to fix the dress.
My dress is all ruined now... I need to get it fixed, quick.
I should ask Lavinia what she thinks.
The funeral's over. I met a few residents who happened to pass by.
Where's Lavinia? There's something I need to tell her.
Just woke up... Most of the wise guys seem to have gone to the theater.
Demetri seems to have something to say.
Things aren't going well. I'll head back to the estate for now.
Looks like my mission from the famiglia is to get that government official there in line.
Time to move. The young man seems to have something to say to me.
Let's get this drunken former classmate back home first.
Someone's waving at me on my way back from the Saluzzo Estate.
This case is about to go to trial. I'll need to head to the archives and read up.
Time to go home after a long day at work.
Capone seems to have something to say.
Time to head over to check on my little musbeast.
Looks like Capone's finished everything I told him to do.
Looks like the people here don’t take kindly to the way I do things.
The moment I get back home, I'm already being given work.
Looks like Emperor wants to talk.
Maybe I'll figure something out if I go back to where I found the radio.
A singer's voice is coming through the radio... Is Sora in trouble?
The ones on the streets are mafiosi, not ordinary civilians.
The prison guards seem to have something to say.
Feeling a bit restless. Maybe I should head to the park to cool down.
Maybe I'll find a restaurant I like before I get to work.
The girl who lived here proudly proclaimed to her parents that she was seeing a young man from a famiglia. The smiles on their faces turned into an unfathomable expression.
Parents always tell their children not to kick tipped-over trash cans. You never know what bad things might roll out.
The Bellones, now mightiest in all the city.
The old streets of Volsinii are either packed with fighting famiglie, or completely empty.
The Rossatis, inheritors of Salvadore's legacy.
'The government is just the cloth draped over Grey Hall's round table.'
TORRE DI COMANDO DEL DISTRETTO CENTRALE SECONDARIO
Control the tower, and you control the city.
Devout worshippers by day, ruthless cutthroats who fight over their slice of the pie by night. On the surface, they appear plenty civilized.
Radio broadcasts are the best ways for Volsinii residents to keep abreast of the latest developments. The TV stations only want you to know what you're allowed to know.
If the wise guys show up, the repairman can do much more than just fix up electronics. He has the telltale callouses on his hands from the abrasion of a bowstring.

Exusiai saw a marking on the door, and without thinking twice, covered it up with graffiti commonly seen in the streets of Lungmen. Consequently, a few days later, an abandoned garage not too far away got blown up.
A place citizens often go to pass the time. The shrubbery leading to a shortcut out of the park has already been trampled flat.
Workers are quickly taking down posters of an up-and-coming lead actor. In private, people whisper about his presence at a famiglia banquet the night before.
Once, a naive wise guy came here bragging about a deal he was about to score. The next day, people found a stiff corpse lying across the front of the doorway.
Even if they have the money, ordinary citizens are reluctant to book a box seat.
Poorer residents live here. A lot of things happen here, but the judges don't pay any extra attention to it.
'Never go into a back alley alone.' Every Siracusan child gets this half-advice, half-plea from their parents.
The owner of the shop claims to be a nobody, but if an establishment never gets any 'solicitations' from a famiglia, everyone already knows what's going on.
Saluzzos never place their bets lightly.
A hospital erected near the courthouse. In addition to the skills typically demanded of their profession, the doctors and nurses also know how to treat lesser-seen explosive and bolt wounds.
Some civilians once watched a judge get pulled into a car and could only fearfully avert their eyes, not daring to peer behind the scenes.
Nobody cares to delve too deeply into why there's a florist next to the prison. The boss simply counts the money.
The coming-of-age ceremony for a mafioso: once in the courthouse, once in the slammer.
A small carwash shop with a clerk of very few words. Business doesn't look too hot; only a few old acquaintances stop by.
Atop these tables, famiglie complete transactions and contests. Such is civilized socialization.
A good place to enjoy the breeze. However, the residents don't get too close to the tree-shaded areas, not since the body of a sanitation worker was found there.
Not everyone is a fan of this cafe's new varieties of coffee. Breaking old rules is a new anomaly.
The buildings along Cittanova's Main Street boast magnificent architecture, but their sharp edges and corners are a bit too sharp for some famiglie's tastes.
The waiters show up only to bring out the menu and serve the food. They know that some conversations are best not overheard.
A rich girl who runs off with Salvadore
A rich girl who runs off with her brother

Had to walk out halfway through. On the way back, I finally figured out what was so weird. Siracusa doesn't even have police! The Lungmen-style gangster flick adapted it to a judge and the wise guys doing drive-by crossbow shootings, which was beyond hilarious. Too bad the boss isn't here, because I'd LOVE for him to get a load of this.
If a Lungmen movie ever turned out this bad, a certain someone would make a fifty-long diss track.

I decided to watch it because of the reviews, so I understand where the polarized ratings come from. I remember watching a movie from Lungmen before that had some nice fights between the gangsters and the cops. What the hell was this?
There are hardly any shows these days that can make me laugh out loud, and they only get fewer and farther between. So just for that alone, nine points!
This eye mask is good at blocking out the light, and the performance did a great job of putting me to sleep.

Quite inferior, even if we're purely speaking from the perspective of a playwright's creative process. There were actually seven main characters, all of which died in the end. Combined with the tragic music, I was left utterly speechless.
I'd rather try nibbling on thistles.
A lot of people started walking out, so I went up to the front. There were lots of exciting fight scenes, so that was good.
You rarely see shows this bad. A complete waste of the time I have after work. I probably should've realized what I was getting into when I saw the long list of companies in the credits.
Never should've been put on stage

Some of my subordinates recommended me this opera. They genuinely believe in the history it recounts, as well as the lofty heights to which it lifts the famiglie. Siracusa's famiglie were never meant to be her saviors. Harboring such illusions in the first place would only serve to destroy the famiglia.

Playwright? Bah, whoever created this doesn't deserve the title. All he knows how to do is grab some pretentious words, some inflammatory ones, and some trendy topics to bait people into paying for it. Slap this hodgepodge together, and call it a finished work!

Shows like this are a quick way to score fame and fortune, and the fact that it's won awards is unsurprising. However, I've been thinking recently–if people get too used to this logic, they’ll just keep talking up whoever’s actually allowed to speak, even if Grey Hall and the famiglie cease to exist.

About halfway through, I decided it'd be more worthwhile to throw a party! Croissant was right, I should've sold apple pie at the door! 
*Edited 3 days later* Huh? Turns out, I went to the wrong number, haha!
After thinking on it, I finally decided to buy another ticket. When would be a good time to invite her to come see it? What a fascinating performance.

Like so many other commenters, I was drawn in by the title. I thought it would be a historical documentary based on primary sources. I was pretty disappointed. If you're looking to study this to improve your writing, I'd stay home instead.
Hahaha, you sure worked your ass off, director!

The title of the play caught my fancy, and I originally planned to study up on the actors, but the story itself was rather disappointing. It should've been about the history and evolution of Siracusa over the years, as well as the conflicts among the famiglie both above-board and behind-the-scenes, but they kept forcing in those strange little praises instead of treating the subject matter seriously. Also, the actors looked pretty lost.

Never expected this play to be so long. I fell asleep halfway through, and got woken up by the people next to me. Almost got kicked out of the theater again. Seeing them trying to fluff up the famiglie like that at the end, not to mention Signora Sicilia, was pretty damned funny.

I heard that the directing team recently won an award. I hope the show actually earned it, and isn’t just another mediocre product propped up to fluff Signora Sicilia. It's not fair to hardworking playwrights.

I didn't really understand what the show was getting at. I wanted to ask someone to explain it to me, but the judge lady who told me to check it out hasn’t come by. I'm not sure how she feels about it in the first place. Maybe I'm not cut out for the opera.

What the playwright seeks to express is evident, but unfortunately, cannot fully do so due to a lack of ability. For example, the brothers' rebellion at the end should've reflected the famiglia's principle of self-interest above all else, yet this was written off as a farce. But having that said, were it not for that bit of expressiveness, the entire opera would've been a complete waste of time.

Next time, I'm going to ask the boss if we can shoot a film about a group of friends, just like this. We’ll move the setting from Lungmen to Siracusa. Dunno about anyone else, but I sure wanna star in that myself★!

Just the same run-of-the-mill stuff I see every day after work. You know what the playwright is trying to convey through these three characters, but unfortunately, they don’t have the skills to pull it off.

The playwright still needs some refinement. Beginning a story with minor characters is a common maneuver. It reflects the changing times, as well as personal development and choices. Unfortunately, the execution didn't pan out in the end.
Like-minded youths always seem to come together. Really takes me back.
Had to leave halfway through because something came up. But, it was still pretty touching to see three like-minded young men. You don’t see such tight-knit fratelli these days.

It’s the lowest wise guy who hates his famiglia, all while clinging to it, yearning for it, until he finally betrays the brothers who were there for him all the way up the ladder just to save his own skin. It’s what it is.

Did the playwright know about the gangsters that got ran out of Siracusa? Their ringleader was a red-haired Vulpo, and the protagonist bore too many similarities to him. Impulsive and arrogant, yet not dislikable at all. The other two brothers, one calm, one brash, matched them perfectly as well!

The playwright's creativity is worth learning from. While everyone else uses serious narratives to tell the stories of the famiglie, this author took the completely opposite approach. Moreover, a number of coincidences occur in this show, but they are presented in a way that always feels natural and not jarring. Very impressive.

Bring your friends! I was almost kicked out for bringing pizza to the door, but we ate it on the spot. The story's really amazing, and I want to get to know the playwright. Acting in a show like this is sure to expand my acting career!

A rarely-seen style. In somewhat ironic fashion, explores the true story of a multi-party struggle, reflecting the dark side of the famiglie's activities. Begins by introducing the backgrounds of a cast of characters, leading to the titular theme, then finally leaving the audience on a suspenseful note. Flows naturally, good show.
Story was very interesting, but those two crooks reminded me of some former subordinates of mine who could never follow instructions. The boss's line stuck with me: 'Just don't hire idiots.'

Unfortunately, I missed the beginning. It's something that happens more and more as you get older. Fortunately, the latter half was exciting. The last few stories all unfolded in the same little room, which was an interesting spin.
Pretty interesting. Not much else to say.

A pretty good show, great for enjoying with friends. It's fun listening to them try to break down the plot. The introductions at the beginning were hard to keep track of; I was fine personally, but someone was about to doze off.

I just happened to stop by after work to kill some time, and I didn't expect the show to be so good. I was blown away when I saw that judge get knocked out and stuffed into the trunk. The author writes unexpected while still realistic twists, carrying a message through. Will recommend to friends.

This is my first time using this new rating system. It was also my first time watching an opera in a theater, which was kind of strange. By the end, I was shouting along with the others. I might have to ask the author myself – what did he choose at the end? To pick up the phone, or to throw away those old rapiers?

Was recommended by a friend, and don't regret it at all. After watching too many shows playing up the greatness of the famiglie, a whole lot of people come to see themselves in the great, heroic mafiosi depicted in those operas. And that's a dangerous thing.

It's clear that the playwright shifted her paradigm once, and this shift elevated the quality of the entire opera to another level, bringing it from a personal story with a heroic narrative style to an evocative Siracusan tale. That’s enough for now. I’ll save rest of my commentary for the arts papers.

An unexpectedly good ending, avoiding falling into common clichés. The youth have the power to go beyond the status quo, and see things from a broader perspective. They are the saplings of our future.

This show was my Siracusan debut! A lot of unexpected things happened along the way, but the final performance turned out pretty good. It looks like the audience enjoyed it too, which makes me very happy!
If things really did end that way, that might've been better for a lot of people
I was eating popcorn in the theater and they kicked me out. Never got to finish.
A satisfying ending, exactly how the story should've ended. It’s basically the image I have in my mind.
My friend starred in the show, so I went to watch her. It was good. Also, goodbye.
Act III was staged successfully. Thankfully, it looks like the events of the preceding period did not interfere with the playwright's work after all. Very much looking forward to your next piece.
Some of the details are realistic, uncannily so. The playwright must have some strong opinions about Texas to come up with an ending like that.

The demise of Famiglia Texas was a result of Siracusa's old order, yet even the fall of such a prominent famiglia did not change anything. The status quo did not change, and the famiglie continued to fight amongst each other. The new Siracusa cannot continue down this path.
A razor-sharp dagger. Its owner took this blade into possession, yet at the same time warned his fellow mafiosi not to take revenge on Leontuzzo Bellone in private.
A strong and durable luggage case. There does not seem to be anything inside it, as there is nothing he needs to take with him.
A delicate, intricate key. Only one such key exists for each box, a method used by the theater manager to ensure the safety of the mafiosi who come here to enjoy the shows.
An exquisite fountain pen. Its user cherishes it very much, and the nib has been honed into a shape most suitable for her after thousands of compositions.
BIGLIETTO PER LA MORTE DI TEXAS

An admission ticket printed with extremely high fidelity. This opera telling the tale of a famous famiglia garnered respectable reviews. Combined with the recent developments in the city, the audience is eagerly awaiting the author's next opus.
An old legal codex. This was the earliest version of Siracusa's legal foundation, and upon it, the entire judicial system Siracusa would deploy.
A short sword that bears testament to his status as a mafioso. A gift from father to son, representing the acknowledgement and expectations of the man who was both his father and don of the famiglia.
Lavinia's Codex. A smudge of another judge's blood can be found on its cover, the finger that brushed against its thorns bearing the same will as hers. The Codex acknowledged his wound.

An old photo. The little girl in it is dressed impeccably in formal attire, her somewhat naive eyes looking not at the camera, but at the person standing beside it. Were it not for the striking similarities, no one would believe that this is an old photo of Lappland.

A radio that suddenly appeared by the side of the road, currently broadcasting opera music. The person who received it was in such a hurry she did not realize she accidentally smashed one of its corners.
As long as events continue to unfold, the playwright will not put her pen down. She also eagerly anticipates what manner of work she will create next.
From this neatly-written resume, one can already tell that its owner is serious and attentive. Its very existence is a form of hope.
The judges have long grown accustomed to the fact that a large number of files will be thrown into the archives with no closure, just like this one.
The judge was even willing to turn against her famiglia to help him, but the customers started questioning whether they should still associate with her while buying flowers.
Officials will not leave behind any sort of evidence that can be used against them in a place like this. Their way of expressing obedience is sometimes as simple as a salutation or a bow.
An unassuming package. Government officials know full well what they will find inside, as well as what they are expected to do.
The buyer knows her friends' tastes well, and purchased all of their favorite foods for them.
The shopkeeper seemed extremely capable. After hearing that Sora belonged to Compagnia dell'alba, those adroit hands became even more circumspect.
Beautiful, exquisite flowers, just enough to cover the stitches of the dress. The one who picked them was careful not to make even the slightest error.
Sora prepared a gift for her long-lost friend, and still seems to be immersed in the joy of their fortuitous reunion.
Wine has many meanings, one of which is acknowledgment.

This is the first time a famiglia's name has formally appeared in the title of a work of art. The people who awaited it did not realize what this signified: that the winds of change had begun to blow.
Unlocked through Leontuzzo Bellone's Solo Action
He turns around, walking away from his old friend. One day, they will find themselves standing against each other.
A sharp dagger, a bottle of rich red wine, and a lingering sorrow.
Everything he did was to see the Bellones become the masters of Siracusa, and he staunchly believed that the Don would lead them there.
In his eyes, there is no difference between civilization and wasteland; however, new developments never fail to pique his interest.
He is here to observe whether there are like-minded individuals who likewise refuse to acclimate to this wasteland masquerading as society.
Unlocked through Lappland Saluzzo's Solo Action
He chose to return to the embrace of violence.
A wanderer left behind by the times, a nobody who exposed the lies.

He could only witness the 'liquidation' that exhilarated him in his dreams, and when he opened his eyes, the reality that presented itself convinced him that civilization had become cowardly and weak.
A new script is still being written. Look forward to the ending.
Come back, o bygone days. You were once so beautiful.
The Columbian famiglie needed to establish a foothold, and could have done all manner of things to accomplish that. If she hadn’t drawn her line in the sand.
The old man heads back to the courthouse to resume his slumber. The old code of law may be changing, but this time, he does not hold the pen.
Guns beget might, order begets law.
Asleep in the courthouse. Only found some people to talk to after waking up.
Unlocked through Cellinia Texas's Solo Action
Her interpretation of 'La Morte di Texas' was not only of her friend's past, but also of her own present and future.
Return to me the moment that should be mine. That is all I ask, nothing more.
When she found out that the theater she worked for was more than meets the eye, her resolve to protect her friends only grew stronger, regardless of what their identities might be.
The wolfcub has grown. All he needs now is more time and experience.
The conflicted young master of the wolfpack, emblematic of an era in flux.

By all logic, the heir serves the bidding of the famiglia. Yet, he has never given up on questioning whether the path set by his father was the correct one, or contemplating the choices he should make.
Instead of practicing the letter of the law, she now would prefer to lift the pen and draft new amendments.
Thorns that grow unyieldingly from beneath the umbral rain; full of scars, yet searching for a way forward.

The word 'justice' should never cross the lips of a famiglia-backed judge, but she has never forgotten the ideals she set for herself when she first stepped into the courthouse, and still stands resolute.
The lone wolf breaks free from the swamp, also relinquishing control of herself, and steps into the wildness.
The wastes, seeking to break free from it all; an empty husk, filled to the brim.
The banished lone wolf who returned to the rainy city. In her eyes, Siracusa is a swamp, and she observes the fates of those who wish to escape it with bated breath.
The lone wolf chose neither to stay nor to leave. She casts her gaze upon Siracusa, angrily urging it to change.
Wrathful, yet calm. Stagnant, yet ever coursing.
The lone wolf who returned to the rainy city. Nothing has changed in seven years. Perhaps, finishing up the tasks she was given one-by-one will let her leave sooner.

At the end of it all, consciousness begins to escape from my mind.
I saw the town I once hated riddled with holes, but this brought me no joy.
The ones left behind <@act.missionTips>continue their search into the wilderness, and find a new conflict</>.
There, I see <@act.missionTips>three wandering giants</>.
I see our mountain.

<@act.missionTips>Beneath the Capitol Spire</>.
<@act.missionTips>Mudrock's</> Sarkaz decide to act.
A tongue of flame laps at the whole town.
But in front of the gates, no more than <@act.missionTips>6 people</> stand guard.

The morning mist compels the quill.
The <@act.missionTips>stones of Wolumonde</> congregate, then disintegrate.
Until <@act.missionTips>20 Colossi are returned to the earth</>,
the land shall know no respite.
